finding: major: tools/apt-repo/build.sh:293 CWE-345 re-signing trusts whatever is already on gh-pages
notes: APT_PINNED_KEY cannot be set from anything an attacker controls in CI. The publish step sets no such variable, the job has no vars/inputs, and no project code runs earlier in that job that could write GITHUB_ENV (only checkout, download-artifact and apt-get run before it). The default resolves through BASH_SOURCE to packaging/apt/vr-telex.asc of the tag checkout, never the site. The signing key must also be in the pinned keyring. gpgv --output parses only the signed text. The Packages hash is checked against that text, and the copy that was hashed is the one parsed. Every pool entry goes through find -print0 under the default -P, so a symlinked pool/ or any subdirectory is refused. Each file must match the listed SHA256. The only unlisted file allowed is a byte-identical input of this run at its own path. A non-empty pool without InRelease is refused unless APT_REPO_BOOTSTRAP=1. dists and dists/stable symlinks are refused, and dists/stable is rebuilt from scratch. Residual risk, not a finding: someone with gh-pages write can roll the site back to an older validly signed state, which drops newer pool files from the next index but cannot add unsigned content; or they can block releases (DoS). Both are acceptable.

finding: minor: .github/workflows/release.yml:101 CWE-284 repository-wide signing secret and ungated v* publish
notes: In code: publish has environment: apt-release. The build job's first step fetches master and checks git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/master, with the tag passed through env and before tools or tests run. publish needs build, so it never runs after a refused tag. test.yml is still pull_request with contents: read and no secrets. The user steps in tools/apt-repo/README.md are complete. They cover: the environment with the owner as reviewer and a tag-type deployment policy 'v*'; moving the secrets to --env and deleting the repository-wide ones, with list checks; a tag ruleset (creation/update/deletion, Admin role id 5 bypass); a gh-pages ruleset with the GitHub Actions integration 15368 bypass; and a test tag off master. Until the owner does steps 1-2 the gate is not in force, because the environment is auto-created without rules and the repository secrets stay readable. That is a user step, not a code defect. Uncertain, depending on GitHub settings I have not seen: whether the Integration 15368 bypass applies to GITHUB_TOKEN pushes in this repository. If it does not, the release push fails closed, so there is no security impact. No new finding from the change.
